svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.8.8.5 Openings in Guards
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.8 STAIRS, RAMPS, LANDINGS, HANDRAILS AND GUARDS
Openings in Guards

g.text: A top rail and intermediate rails.
Not in between: a child can get

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Openings through guards prevent the passage of a
100 mm (3 15/16″) sphere
Except as permitted in Sentences (3) and (4).
Triangular openings formed by stair risers, stair
treads and the bottom element of a required guard
prevent the passage of a 150 mm (5⅞″) sphere
Except guards that serve industrial occupancies.
Industrial occupancies, except where serving
storage garages: a top railing and one or more
horizontal intermediate rails, with openings that
prevent the passage of a 535 mm (21 1/16″) sphere
Guards not required by Article 9.8.8.1., other
than in industrial occupancies: openings prevent
the passage of a 100 mm sphere, or permit the
passage of a 200 mm (7⅞″) sphere
Why
Children can fall through guards, and can get their
head stuck in openings between 100 mm and 200 mm.
Industrial buildings differ because children are
unlikely to be present except under strict
supervision.
Drawn: a stair guard with a raked bottom rail. Spheres and elevations are drawn to scale with their guards.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.8.8.5. (page 9-40), with Notes A-9.8.8.5.(1) and (3) and A-9.8.8.5.(4).
